findings.title: Password form submits over HTTP
findings.description: A password-bearing form submits to cleartext HTTP.
findings.impact: Credentials may be exposed to interception.
findings.remediation: Use HTTPS-only authentication endpoints and redirect/block cleartext access.

findings.title: Preflight reflects untrusted origin with credentials enabled
findings.description: An OPTIONS preflight response reflected the synthetic untrusted Origin and enabled credentials.
findings.impact: If sensitive endpoints share this policy, untrusted browser origins may be able to read responses in a credentialed context.
findings.remediation: Return only explicitly allow-listed origins; review credential policy and allowed methods/headers.
findings.evidence_summary: Preflight Origin was reflected while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials was true.

findings.title: CORS origin reflection detected
findings.description: The response reflected an arbitrary test Origin value in Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
findings.impact: Origin reflection can enable unintended cross-origin access when combined with sensitive resources or credentials.
findings.remediation: Use a strict allow-list and validate origins server-side rather than reflecting arbitrary Origin values.

findings.title: Sensitive-looking page lacks Cache-Control evidence
findings.description: A sensitive-looking URL does not expose a restrictive Cache-Control policy.
findings.impact: Shared/private caching could retain sensitive material depending on framework/proxy behavior.
findings.remediation: Review caching policy and explicitly control storage for authenticated/sensitive responses.
findings.evidence_summary: No Cache-Control header on sensitive-looking path.

findings.title: Third-party script without Subresource Integrity
findings.description: One or more third-party scripts lack an integrity attribute in the observed markup.
findings.impact: If the third-party source is compromised or changes unexpectedly, script content may change without an SRI check.
findings.remediation: For stable third-party assets, consider SRI plus crossorigin; use CSP and dependency governance as defense in depth.

findings.title: CSRF protection not obvious in state-changing form
findings.description: No commonly named CSRF token field was observed. This is a review candidate, not proof of a CSRF flaw.
findings.impact: State-changing requests may require server-side CSRF defenses.
findings.remediation: Verify framework/token/header-based CSRF controls for state-changing operations.
findings.evidence_summary: No common CSRF token field name detected.

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy not observed
findings.description: No Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy response header was observed on HTML.
findings.impact: Cross-origin window relationships may be less isolated than a highly isolated application expects.
findings.remediation: Review whether same-origin or same-origin-allow-popups isolation is appropriate for this application.
findings.evidence_summary: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy absent; applicability depends on app behavior.

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy not observed
findings.description: No Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy response header was observed on HTML.
findings.impact: Cross-origin resource embedding policy is implicit rather than explicitly declared.
findings.remediation: Assess whether same-origin, same-site, or cross-origin resource policy fits the product.
